title: Flip Swap, Bento Grain, Grown Type, Elastic Drag & Anchored Palette
description: Five live drops: a concentric 3D testimonial flip, a grained masonry bento grid, grass-grown headline type, an elastic drag-ripple text toy, and a Popover API + anchor-positioned command palette.

drops.title: Concentric Testimonial Swap
drops.description: Five testimonial cards flip in 3D with an elastic overshoot, staggered from the outer edges inward (or reversed).
drops.concept: Two stacked faces per card swap on an interval: the outgoing face rotates away on the X axis while the incoming face rotates in from -90deg with a back/elastic easing curve, scaling up from 0.7 to 1 under a CSS perspective. Stagger delay is computed per card from its distance to the row's center, so the ripple can run edges-in or center-out.
drops.source: Codrops — 'Building an Animated Testimonial Hero Using the GSAP Timeline and Dynamic CMS Data' (Jonas Arleth)

interaction.mouse: watch the auto-cycle, or use the debug panel to swap manually
interaction.click: Swap Now button forces an immediate swap
interaction.touch: auto-cycles the same way on mobile

drops.title: Generative Masonry Bento
drops.description: A four-column CSS masonry grid of procedurally-generated gradient panels with grain, each a different aspect ratio.
drops.concept: Each tile is a canvas painted with a randomized linear gradient, soft radial highlight blobs and a pixel-level grain pass, seeded with a small PRNG so palettes reshuffle deterministically. Tiles sit in a CSS multi-column masonry layout; hovering slides up a glass overlay chip showing a category label and a fake source link, echoing the classic image-bento hover reveal without needing real photography.
drops.source: Aceternity UI — 'Masonry Bento Grid With Images'

interaction.mouse: hover any tile to reveal its overlay chip
interaction.click: reshuffle button generates a new grid; palette buttons swap the color scheme
interaction.touch: tap a tile to reveal the overlay

drops.title: Overgrown Type
drops.description: Grass blades sampled along each glyph's top contour, grown in with staggered spring easing and left swaying in the wind.
drops.concept: The headline is rendered once to an offscreen canvas; scanning each pixel column for its topmost opaque pixel produces a 'skyline' contour. Blade origins are seeded along that contour, each with a random length, lean and phase, and grow in with an ease-out-back curve staggered by horizontal position when the headline scrolls into view. After growing, blades sway continuously via a sine function scaled by a wind slider.
drops.source: Mandy Michael — growing-grass variable-font experiment (CodePen), reimplemented without a custom font file

interaction.mouse: scroll each headline into view to trigger growth; click to regrow
interaction.click: tap any headline to regrow its blades
interaction.touch: tap to regrow, same as click

drops.title: FlexiString
drops.description: Drag any letter and the stretch ripples outward through its neighbors with distance falloff; release for an elastic spring-back.
drops.concept: Each character is its own span. Dragging one maps the pointer delta directly to a squash-and-stretch scale on that letter; a distance-based falloff (by character-index offset) applies a decayed copy of the same transform to nearby letters, producing a visible ripple. On release, the Web Animations API tweens every letter back to its rest transform with a back/elastic easing curve, staggered slightly by distance from the drag origin for a whip-like recoil.

interaction.mouse: click and drag any single letter
interaction.click: drag then release to trigger the spring-back
interaction.touch: drag a letter with one finger

drops.title: Anchored Command Palette
drops.description: A ⌘K command palette and a toast stack with zero positioning JavaScript, built on the Popover API and CSS anchor positioning.
drops.concept: The trigger button declares `popovertarget`, and the palette panel is `popover="auto"` — the browser handles show/hide, focus management, light-dismiss and top-layer promotion for free, with a stylable ::backdrop. CSS anchor positioning (`anchor-name` on the trigger, `position-anchor` + `anchor()` on the panel) pins the palette directly beneath its trigger without any JS measuring code; a plain fixed-position fallback keeps it usable if the browser doesn't yet support anchor positioning. Executing a command spawns a toast into a fixed bottom-right stack that auto-dismisses.
drops.source: BuildMVPFast — 'The HTML Popover API: Native Modals Without a Library'

interaction.mouse: click the trigger or press Ctrl/Cmd+K to open the palette
interaction.click: click a command to run it and spawn a toast
interaction.touch: tap the trigger button to open on mobile
